edbDesc: The tendency of a solid material to slowly move or deform permanently under the influence of stresses. A result of long term exposure to levels of stress that are below the yield strength of the material. Creep is more severe in materials that are subjected to heat for long periods, and near the melting point. Creep always increases with temperature. The rate of deformation is a function of the material properties, exposure time, exposure temperature and the applied structural load.
title: Creep
pickWhy: A slow failure mode that designers fight, not an effect that does a job.
